simple: Labels are how you show words and pictures in your game's UI. A `TextLabel` is a box with text in it, and an `ImageLabel` is a box with a picture in it. You can put them on the player's screen or on the side of a part, like a poster. Players can look at labels, but they cannot click them; for that you would use a button.
analogy: Labels are like the signs and stickers in a store: they tell you things and show pictures, but pressing them does nothing.
keyPoints: `TextLabel` is the main way to show text in a game, and `ImageLabel` shows a picture.
For on-screen labels: add a `ScreenGui` to `StarterGui`, then add a `TextLabel` or `ImageLabel` inside it.
For labels on a part: add a `SurfaceGui` to the part, then add the label inside the `SurfaceGui`.
If you cannot see a label on a part, try a different `Face` on the `SurfaceGui`.
Images must be imported to Studio as assets before an `ImageLabel` can show them.
Images stretch to fit the box but look best at their original size.
`ImageColor3` tints the image, `ImageTransparency` fades it, and `BackgroundTransparency` set to 1 hides the box behind it.

terms.GuiObject: Any 2D UI piece, like a label, button, or frame.
terms.asset: A file uploaded to Roblox, like an image, with its own ID.
terms.native resolution: The image's real size in pixels. A 256 by 256 image looks sharpest when shown at 256 by 256.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. 0 is solid, 1 is invisible, 0.5 is half see-through.
terms.ImageColor3: A color mixed over the image. White leaves it unchanged; red makes it reddish.
terms.SurfaceGui: A container that puts UI onto one face of a part.

example.title: Show a coin counter on screen
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

-- A ScreenGui holds on-screen UI
local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Name = "CoinGui"
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 50) -- 200 pixels wide, 50 tall
label.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 20) -- 20 pixels from top-left
label.BackgroundTransparency = 1 -- hide the box, keep the text
label.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 215, 0) -- gold
label.TextSize = 32
label.Text = "Coins: 0"
label.Parent = screenGui
explain: We find this player's `PlayerGui`, where on-screen UI lives.
We create a `ScreenGui` to hold our label.
We create a `TextLabel`, size it, and place it near the top-left corner.
We hide the background box, color the text gold, and set the text.
Later, you can change `label.Text` to show the new coin count.

watchOut: Labels cannot be clicked. If you need clicks, use a `TextButton` or `ImageButton`.
An `ImageLabel` with a blank `Image` shows only a plain box. Make sure you set a real image asset ID.
If the white box behind your text looks ugly, set `BackgroundTransparency` to 1.
